News highlights 23rd November 2026

_LOCAL NEWS_🇱🇰

IMF to consider Sri Lanka’s seventh programme review on December 2
The Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is scheduled to consider Sri Lanka’s Article IV Consultation and Seventh Review under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) programme on December 2, potentially paving the way for the release of approximately US$345 million in funding.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4z3wuys8

Private credit growth cools to 21.8% but still runs high: CBSL
The Central Bank of Sri Lanka’s (CBSL) May tightening is showing up in market interest rates. Private sector credit growth is slowing but remains high, which is part of the reason for this week’s second rate hike.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4bxdb8kk

Sri Lanka central bank to get marketable bonds next year to mop up liquidity
Sri Lanka’s central bank will gain a large stock of marketable Treasury bonds starting March next year, giving it a market-based tool to permanently absorb excess cash in the banking system without issuing its own securities, Deputy Governor Chandranath Amarasekara said.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4v3yvasd

Sinopec retreat affects refinery future plans
Sri Lanka’s proposed US$3.7 billion Hambantota Oil Refinery project with China’s Sinopec has stalled prompting the government to seek alternatives, to build a 200,000-barrel-per-day facility.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/hx4c4m3y

Construction Support Centre launched ahead of Rs 2 trillion budget
Sri Lanka has launched the ‘Builders’ gateway’ Construction Industry Support Centre to address administrative bottlenecks, project delays and other challenges affecting the construction sector, as the Government prepares to implement a Rs 2 trillion (Rs 2,000 billion) development budget for 2027, the Department of Government Information (DGI) said on Friday (20).
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4davpwc2

CDA to set minimum export prices for coconut products
The Coconut Development Authority (CDA) is moving to introduce fixed minimum declared export prices for coconut shell charcoal and fresh nuts in a bid to maximise foreign exchange earnings across Sri Lanka’s coconut export sector.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/mua75b2m

Sri Lanka hits 2mn tourists for 3rd conservative year
Sri Lanka crossed two million tourist arrivals for the third consecutive year on November 20, three days later than in 2025, with a sharp slump in March and April, still leaving the cumulative arrivals behind last year’s pace, despite the strong growth from India, the official data showed.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/bp9a6add

_Global News_🌎

US futures bounce while Asia markets brace for AI wipeout
US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, while Asian markets slid and authorities around the region readied support measures after a ​withering wipeout last week for tech and chip stocks at the centre ‌of the AI boom.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/4s794s34

Saudi Arabia, Bahrain report new attacks as Iran says it remains open to a deal with U.S.
Saudi Arabia and Bahrain reported attacks by Iran-linked forces over the weekend, as Iran’s foreign minister said his government remains open to a deal to end the war with the U.S.
Reference - https://tinyurl.com/3bdr8jr4
